kinds.d: Horse meat sold whole or as any cut, including raw slices for eating raw.

x.d: Thin-sliced raw horsemeat sashimi eaten with garlic, ginger and soy; Kumamoto, Japan's leading producer, counts it a signature dish.

kinds.d: Meat of North American bison, ranched and sold whole or as steaks, roasts and mince.

x.d: Bison of the plains subspecies, ranched for meat and sold as ribeye and other steaks.

kinds.d: Lean meat of wild kangaroos harvested under licence in Australia, sold as fillets, steaks, mince and sausages.
Dark, lean meat of the farmed ostrich, sold mainly as fillets and steaks.
Pale, mild meat of farmed crocodiles and alligators, the tail being the prized cut.

x.d: The most tender alligator cut, from farms in Florida and Louisiana.
White or pink tail meat of farm-reared crocodiles, the main cut beside leg, torso and jaw.

kinds.d: Camel meat, like coarse beef; the hump, brisket, ribs and loin are preferred.
The hind legs of edible frogs, sold raw or frozen.
The meat of turtles sold to eat.
Insects sold to eat, frozen, dried, roasted or ground to powder.

x.d: Insect species approved as novel foods in the EU, in frozen, dried and powder forms.

kinds.a: butcher's box · meat subscription box · mixed fresh meats
kinds.d: A box of raw meats from several animals, bought once or by subscription, no one meat making up half its weight.

brands.d: US meat delivery subscription service shipping beef, pork, chicken and seafood.

notes: Six old horse kinds (horse meat, ribeye, tenderloin, sirloin, flank, ground) merged into Horse meat with cuts as types; Basashi became an archetype. Wood bison not attested on a retrieved page, so only plains bison is an archetype. Turtle meat and frogs' legs stay kind-level with old sources. Mixed fresh meats became Meat box (no models).
